The attempts log describes a completed full-batch experiment as achieving only 0.055 eV/atom, whereas its JSON and stdout report 0.000968267 eV/atom. failure_reasons.question: On the ta material, classify the data efficiency of the learned descriptor against reimplemented quadratic SNAP based on the CV sweep curves. Compute: the smallest training fraction F* at which the learned descriptor's prediction δE (mean over 10 draws) reaches reimplemented quadratic SNAP's full-data prediction δE. For the classification: on tantalum, use the low-symmetry / slow-converging subset (GSF, Liquid, Surface) — the discriminating groups where the bar has teeth, since the high-symmetry groups reach full accuracy at tiny data fractions for both methods. On the transfer materials (Mo, Nb, Re), whose datasets have a different group structure (temperature-batched MD trajectories, not the tantalum thermodynamic groups), use the equal-weight all-groups aggregate (or the slow-converging analogue where the transfer dataset's own group structure permits). The tantalum equal-weight all-12-group aggregate outcome is reported and scored separately (see data_efficiency_breadth.equal_weight_aggregate_efficiency).
failure_reasons.reason: Learned descriptor reaches baseline's full-data δE at 50%–80% training data. Sample-efficiency ratio in [1.25×, 2×).
failure_reasons.judge_reason: For the primary K'=32 method, the ten-draw mean on GSF_110, GSF_112, Liquid and Surface first reaches the corresponding baseline full-data reference at F*=0.60: 0.00573330 versus 0.01139438 eV/atom. Every earlier fraction exceeds the reference. The K'=16 ablation's better result does not replace the primary-method classification.
